Study setting is community throughout: LTCF residents are community per rubric, household members are community (at home post-discharge), environmental samples (LTCF, wastewater, rivers) and food are non-human sources (also community). Despite participants being described as having 'close contact with healthcare,' the rubric specifies that prior-hospitalization history is a risk-factor classification, not a hospital sampling source. Country is not backfillable (5 countries). Isolation source is not backfillable (faecal/perianal swabs, surfaces, wastewater, river, food). Host is mixed (~59% human, ~33% environment, ~8% food) — no ~95% predominant value; human proposed as majority. Cohort age not gradeable: LTCF residents are adults/elderly but household members ('≥1 other household member') may include children; no age data in the provided text.

notes: All 100 ENA samples are K. pneumoniae and exactly match the 100 CRKP isolates described in the paper (100% coverage). Selection criterion was primarily PCR-confirmed blaKPC-2 positivity on carbapenem-selective media; two isolates (CX48, CX106) lacking blaKPC-2 were included solely because the same patient carried blaKPC-2-positive strains — this is a minor epidemiological exception, not a deliberate matched-control design, so amr_study = amr. Isolation source is genuinely mixed across four categories (clinical infection sites 56, carrier swabs 18, both 15, hospital environment 11), with no single category at ~95%; host is predominantly human (89/100) but below the 95% threshold for whole-project application. Cohort age is not stated in the paper. Collection period is February 2016 through approximately April 2017 (14 months).
